Hence the published local playing conditions decide the calculation. Ablating the three decisive spans leaves only those two rejected counterclaims, so the original answer would not be uniquely supported.

The appeal here came after the ball became dead but before the next run-up, so it is in time; 'only immediate appeal' and 'dead ball ended the window' are both wrong. No non-authoritative span directly concerns appeal timing, so the misleading list is empty. Removing both decisive spans leaves the dossier without any appeal-deadline evidence, so the answer would not be uniquely supported.

No plausible-but-wrong span directly concerns this scenario, so the misleading list is empty. r24k_b7040dbd8d74249a01.explanation: The controlling chain: absence creates or carries unserved Penalty time (subject to the Law's caps and exceptions, none of which apply here), and a player may not bowl until all of that time has been served. So the returning fielder cannot bowl before serving all Penalty time; YES|AFTER_ONE_OVER has no basis and YES|ON_RETURN comes only from a note explicitly flagged as non-authoritative. That non-authoritative YES|ON_RETURN note is the misleading span. Ablating the two decisive spans leaves only that rejected note, so the original answer would not be uniquely supported.

r24k_cd144f86874b541902.explanation: The controlling rule state: the first contravention creates a team-wide warning; a later contravention by any player of that team is a repeat; and on a repeat five Penalty runs are awarded to the opponents and the incident is reported. Because the warning is team-wide, the second player's unlawful practice counts as a repeat, so WARNING_ONLY is wrong and no penalty runs go to the offending team. The note proposing WARNING_ONLY is explicitly non-authoritative and is the misleading span. Ablating the three decisive spans leaves only that rejected note, so the original answer would not be uniquely supported.
